newsitem.title: USA: Gillette shares recover, Merrill lends hand.
newsitem.headline: Gillette shares recover, Merrill lends hand.

text.p: Shares of Gillette Co, which tumbled last week after the giant U.S. consumer products company guided analysts estimates down, recouped lost ground on Tuesday as Merrill Lynch raised its rating on the stock.

Gillette's stock was up 2-1/4 to 85-1/4, pulling higher after an earnings announcement on Friday which sparked widespread fears about the fate of U.S. corporate profits and sent the Dow industrials spiraling lower.

The stock was bolstered by Merrill Lynch analysts Heather Hay and Deepak Raj, who raised their intermediate-term rating on Gillette to buy from accumulate, stressing Gillette's reasonable valuation and excellent fundamentals.

"We entered mid-97 concerned that earnings expectations might have been too optimistic, but with the range recently adjusted this has been discounted by the market," Hay said in a research note. She said estimates were now realistic.

Shares of other personal consumer products companies rallied alongside Gillette. Colgate-Palmolive gained 1-3/8 to 67-3/8, Procter & Gamble was up 1-3/4 to 136-3/4 and Clorox Co rose 2-3/16 to 135-1/8.

Last week, Gillette guided analysts to the lower end of an earlier range of $2.55 to $2.60 per share. It said its Braun unit had been hurt by weakness in Japan and Germany, two key markets for the unit.
But Hays and Raj said Gillette had excellent fundamentals and a compelling valuation, and that the stock's recent price weakness was overdone.
"We believe top-line growth will recover to a double-digit secular rate in 1998," the analysts said.
Salomon Brothers also reinitiated coverage on Gillette shares on Tuesday with a buy rating, seeing accelerated sales growth after a transition year in 1997.

"Gillette remains the most prolific new product company in our personal care universe with strong growth in its megabrands like Sensor Excel and Sensor Excel for women," Salomon analyst Diana Temple said in a research note.
In 1997, Gillette had digested inventory reductions in blades, reduced distributor sales at its Duracell acquisition and flatness at Braun, she said.
Gillette said on Tuesday its Duracell unit was exiting the rechargable computer battery market. This would affect 236 employees at its Waterbury, Conn. site, it said.
